messages.content:
Two readers answered the same question about machines at work. Reader A used facts taken from a fact
store; each fact comes with the sentence it was taken from. Reader B read the documents directly and points at
sentences. Decide which answer the evidence supports. Use only the evidence shown; do not use what you know.

Rules:
- An answer is supported only if its evidence states it for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the
  same article and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline, the same condition the question
  states). Evidence about a neighbouring subject does not support an answer.
- When the two rest on texts of different rank, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's
  manual, then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.)
  wins over a ministerial decree (DM). A wording corrected by a corrigendum replaces the original wording.
- For a list, prefer the answer whose items are each stated by the evidence and that leaves none out.
- If reader B found nothing, decide only whether A's evidence really states A's answer for the exact subject.
- "same" means the two answers say the same thing. "neither" means neither answer is supported.
Return JSON only: {"reasoning": "two or three short sentences", "choice": "A" | "B" | "same" | "neither"}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: Who is considered the manufacturer after a substantial modification of machinery?

Answer A: "The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer under Art. 18 of the Regulation, and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility; a non-professional user modifying machinery solely for its own use is not considered a manufacturer."
Under Article 18 of the Regulation, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification (one that affects the safety of only the machinery or a related product in an assembly) becomes subject to the manufacturer's obligations and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility; a non-professional user modifying machinery for its own use is excluded.
Evidence of A:
- non-professional user modifying machinery for own use: becomesManufacturer = shall not be considered to be a manufacturer (condition: for his or her own use) | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10." [REG, Art. 18]
- natural or legal person carrying out substantial modification: hasObligation = shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 (condition: if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery) | sentence: "Article 18 Other cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product or, if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery, for that affected machinery or related product, as demonstrated in the risk assessment." [REG, Art. 18]
- person who carries out substantial modification: hasObligation = ensure and declare on its sole responsibility | sentence: "The person who carries out the substantial modification shall in particular, but without prejudice to other obligations set out in Article 10, ensure and declare on its sole responsibility that the machinery or related product concerned is in conformity with the applicable requirements of this Regulation and shall apply the relevant conformity assessment procedure as provided in Article 25 (2), (3) and (4) of this Regulation." [REG, Art. 18]

Answer B: "The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery is considered the manufacturer, except a non-professional user modifying machinery for their own use."
Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, the natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery becomes the manufacturer and takes on the manufacturer's obligations under Article 10. A non-professional user who modifies their own machinery for their own use is excluded.
Evidence of B:
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product" [REG, Art. 18]
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10." [REG, Art. 18]

response.text: {"reasoning": "Both answers rest on the same Art. 18 of the Regulation and say the same core thing: the person who carries out the substantial modification is the manufacturer, and a non-professional user modifying for own use is excluded. A adds the ensure-and-declare conformity duty and the limit to affected machinery, both stated in Art. 18, but these are extra detail rather than a different answer.", "choice": "same"}
